purpose: Show that boundary contact and crossing in ordinal mismatch governance do not collapse into numeric thresholds, units, or topological claims.

counterexample_case.label: Boundary contact without equal numeric meaning
counterexample_case.setup: Trace T1 approaches and contacts BDRY_01 from LOW_MISMATCH under S_boundary_01 and r_a_03. Trace T2 contacts the same declared boundary after a reference rebinding that changes the admissibility context but not the ordinal-only status of the trace.
counterexample_case.result: Both traces are boundary contacts, but they do not determine equal magnitude, equal interval size, or a numeric boundary thickness.

blocked_readings: A boundary contact is not a unit interval.
A boundary crossing is not a spatial crossing.
A boundary persistence trace is not a topological invariant.
ADMISSIBILITY_BREAK is not a metric maximum.
Boundary states do not imply scalar thresholds.
forbidden_inference: Boundary behavior does not imply numeric distance.
Boundary behavior does not imply physical phase change.
Boundary behavior does not imply topology.
Boundary behavior does not imply role symmetry.
Boundary behavior does not modify RT_core.

non_claims: Does not prove impossibility of all metrics.
